works.title: The Oracle
works.description: An anti-empire/anti-rentier economic critique grounded in spiritual practice (communion, presence, illustrated through dogs, relationships, poker) that develops an oracle mythology and moral algorithm. The work explores how empires control commons (air, water, networks, knowledge) and proposes architectural solutions that distribute economic gains rather than centralizing them. Includes launch and distribution strategy with predicted political fallout.
works.quote: If the rules let empire fence off what only works as a commons—air, water, networks, knowledge—then corruption is baked in.
